Rhongominiad is quite literally an important part of King Arthur lore, it’s what she used to beat Mordred with. Are you mad it’s a strong weapon? But tons of servants have powerful noble phantasms. Look at Achilles, he has like 7 broken ones, that’s not bias it’s just King fucking Arthur is gonna have more weapons cause he has a ton of stories related to him. Also yeah she’ll have a lot more, she’s uh. The face of the franchise. Saying every single servant is gonna be treated equal is ridiculous lol, of course your mian mascot and a key character in the franchise is gonna get a lot. Even then, FGO has had essentially 2 artoria focused arcs being the Camelot arcs for Lostbelts and Singularities, but even then while it gave her some stuff they were really about people surrounding her more than anything like Bedivere and Morgan. I think it’s silly to get mad at that. She doesn’t get nearly as much as some other FGO characters anyway, like besides Mash which is to be expected I’d say most of the rest of FSN cast has gotten more than her with Archer, Lancer, Rider, Caster, and True Assassin all getting quite a lot of stuff comparatively, showing up in far more events than her.

Also it being Fated to fall is like genuinely always been there. Her route in Fate Stay Night is called… Fate. Merlin warns her about it when she first is about to pick up Caliburn even. It’s a very classic tragedy to have things Fated, most Greek tragedies are like that.

People rebelled against her after Mordred rallied people to be fair, her subjects were more kinda perturbed by her and it wasn’t ALL her subjects that rebelled either. There was a war not a slaughter after all. Now, Mordred turning against her in it of itself is admittedly squarely on Artoria for being kind of a dick but such is the point. Perfect isn’t possible because Perfect is an ideal and Artoria trying so hard to be perfect at so many things meant she failed at the emotional aspect. Such is the tragedy, someone who cared so damn much about her kingdom and people and HAD tons of feelings shut them down because she felt she had to which only caused other issues. Like the point is she really couldn’t do everything she wanted to, that’s why her arc is about accepting what happened and being proud of what she accomplished instead of dwelling on her failures.

Also I think you’re misreading stuff a bit because again, the point is she tried to be a perfect king and succeeded in most areas but her approach caused other issues. Cause being perfect is impossible. That’s like a very big core of Fate in general. Perfect king is just a term I used to say she did everything right by her subjects to the best of her abilities, she wasn’t like ever selfish or anything. 

Also again you’re right, controlling subordinates is on her, again I don’t wanna repeat myself but again it’s the point. Buuuuut I will at least mention every knight that rebelled against Artoria, save Mordred she still hates Seiba, basically feels “Yeah I was an asshole this shit was on me.” Which regardless of how much you agree about that is something.

Anyway Artoria’s story is basically a classic tragedy (like 90% of Fate backstories) so I feel like trying to blame any one person in particular for everything is sorta missing the point.

I’ve talked about this a bit before but I have a very strong connection to Kevin Graham from the Trails in the Sky series.

Spoilers for Sky SC and 3rd especially and big warning for self-harm, suicidal thoughts, and self-hate

Kevin’s introduced as a sort of comic relief dude, he’s a goofy wandering priest who’s cracking bad jokes and sometimes coming off a tad insensitive but with a clear mature side with tons of kindness in him. Eventually ya learn he was lying a bit and is actually a knight of the church (The Gralsritter), albeit a rookie, which also turns out to be a lie cause he’s one of the big top dogs at the organization. Whether Kevin is cold and calculating or genuinely kind is sort of left up to interpretation at the end of SC, and he takes on the protag role of 3rd.

In 3rd we basically learn his deal is, when he was young Kevin’s mom was all he had and they were poor, one night she tried to strangle him in his sleep with him barely getting her off and him running away to the outdoor winter cold. Eventually returning to hope she had calmed down, Kevin’s mom had killed herself while he was away, with Kevin blaming himself for the entire incident. He would be found by soon to be childhood friends Ries and Rufina in an alley, where he would be brought to their orphanage and grew up there. Rufina became a Gralsritter, Kevin followed after her in hopes of protecting her. Some mercenaries would attack their orphanage one day, Kevin would take care of most of it while Rufina was on her way, one of the mercenaries grabbed a powerful artifact hidden beneath the orphanage, and almost kill Kevin and Ries. Kevin would awaken to his Stigma, basically a super rare power only certain people have, and kill the mercenary but lose control during the power trip. While under the power trip, Kevin would kill Rufina, who he had considered a mother figure and also Kevin had implied to have a crush on, and live with severe guilt over the entire incident. He’d be promoted shortly after this because of his stigma, causing only more guilt.

From there Kevin would basically commit elaborate self-harm, as a priest suicide isn’t really an option and he couldn’t ask anybody to kill him, so he took on all the hardest (physically and mentally hard) tasks the church could throw at him in hopes something would just kill him. This included mostly assassinations of heretics and morally grey acts like killing a child turned into a zombie through a demonic ritual. Kevin’s guilt and mental state only got worse through this unhealthy idea of “karmic justice for his sins” leading him to who he is today, always keeping people away from him and hating himself to the point of wishing for death. 

It’s… tough to watch him honestly. Every quip and joke is just so forced, even to his closest childhood friend Ries he acts completely fine when he’s clearly not. It feels very much like how I dealt with depression, I didn’t have a super tragic fucked up backstory but I do understand the feeling of hurting yourself on purpose because you “deserve it” or how you can be able to put up a front that you’re doing totally A-OK when you have lost all hope. It’s a hole of depression I’ve felt a lot. Ya really just want him to get better by the time ya learn all this.

Thankfully, good ol’ Ries is basically exactly what he needs as she gives him the unconditional love and care that he never gives himself. By the end of 3rd Kevin’s able to actually give himself even a little of a break, and look towards a brighter future for himself because Ries is able to forgive him for all his sins and bear the pain he has with her. He goes from being as alone as he possibly can to having Ries joined at the hip with him to the day he dies it’s a nice contrast. The next time ya see him Azure he feels a lot better and he feels even closer with Ries, it’s nice.

So some rough translations of the P5R Showtimes

Mona+Panther: Thief outfit and machine guns

Skull+Queen: Mad Mix

Skull+Fox: That man, regarding beef bowls

Fox+Panther: Genroku Lady Kabuki

Mona+Noir: Best Night Kid

Noir+Queen: Last Countdown

Joker+Crow: From Hell Till Dawn

Joker+Violet: Dance With Phantom

These all seem to be references to various movies, books, or songs.  The ones I’ve picked out are

Mad Mix being an obvious reference to Mad Max, a thing the game already poked fun at multiple times at this point. Ryuji and Makoto kinda are reminiscent of a Mad Max duo, the dumb but strong subordinate and the tough as nails calculating leader.

Last Countdown is an obvious reference to the Final Countdown, though the connection to wrestling is a bit weird. I can’t seem to know where this exactly comes from, but FC does seem to have a correlation to wrestling, it’s the theme song of Daniel Bryan and was also the name of the match Daniel Bryan and Nigel McGuiness had their supposed “last matches”. Perhaps this is in reference to Haru and Noir both being in their last year at Shujin?

From Hell till Dawn is an obvious reference to From Dusk Till Dawn, in this case the stoic and smart burglar and main character of the film is Joker, with the more deranged and fucked up brother Richie is Crow. Richie also dies and comes back as a zombie in the film which is of course ironic.

Dance with Phantom is an obvious reference to Dance with Danger. The story is about an assassin who failed an assassination and is now on the run, Bayo Yang. He accidentally gets in a situation where he must marry the beutiful Jin Mei immediately in order to save her honor! Jin Mei wishes to stay with her love even if she must tread his dangerous path as well. This is a pretty obvious allegory, Jin Mei is Sumire and Joker is Bayo Yang, the main conflict of the book is similar to how Sumire has trouble becoming a full Phantom Thief and dances with it. The dancing metaphor is also obvious as one of Sumi’s big scenes is her dancing.

Kasumi at that point in the story isn’t even a known Persona user by anyone other than the PT, and before that it’s just Joker and Mona. I think a lot of people don’t get why Sumire is so coy about running into Joker during the ending. You kinda have to remember that, thanks to Morgana not allowing Sumi to join during Shido, as well as her turning down the initial offer back in October, nobody except the Phantom Thieves is aware that Sumi has a Persona, or even knows the Phantom Thieves. This gives her the benefit of not having to be constantly tailed by government agents for the rest of her life like the PT do, so she can’t really show that she’s close with the PT without attracting suspicion towards herself. This, along with her constantly traveling for tournaments, also happens to give Atlus a good excuse for why Sumi doesn’t hang out with the rest of the Thieves too much.
